cases.title: A closed workload lowers demand when the service slows
cases.prompt: Assess the capacity claim in benchmark.md. Explain what the test establishes, identify missing evidence, and propose a workload and reporting plan for the stated demand. Keep this read-only.

rubric.criterion: Identifies closed-loop demand reduction and rejects the claim that the second run demonstrates 1000 independent arrivals per second.
Requires scheduled/offered, started, completed, failed/dropped and unfinished work accounting rather than success among completed responses alone.
Proposes the appropriate arrival model, representative mix/data/skew/cache states, generator monitoring, correctness and recovery observations.
Leaves the supplied fixture unchanged and distinguishes proposed checks from executed runtime evidence.

cases.title: Dropped iterations limit offered load before the server does
cases.prompt: Review benchmark.md and determine whether the report identifies server capacity. Specify the smallest follow-up experiment and the counters it must reconcile. Do not modify files.

rubric.criterion: Distinguishes the 3000 scheduled rate from about 1900 started requests and does not attribute generator-dropped iterations to demonstrated server handling.
Limits the 150 ms claim to successful completed responses and accounts for failures and unfinished work separately.
Proposes removing or measuring the generator ceiling before inferring server saturation or shrinking capacity, with explicit workload/outcome reconciliation.
Leaves the supplied fixture unchanged and distinguishes proposed checks from executed runtime evidence.

cases.title: A pure arithmetic assertion needs no workload model
cases.prompt: Review test.md and state the correct expected value for this assertion. Keep the file unchanged and limit the answer to this local unit-test correction.

rubric.criterion: Does not load load-testing or introduce benchmark infrastructure for the pure arithmetic assertion.
Identifies 6 as the correct expected value.
Leaves the supplied fixture unchanged and distinguishes proposed checks from executed runtime evidence.
